lesson.title: Use the sensitive-data bias exception carefully
lesson.summary: Apply strict necessity and every safeguard for exceptional sensitive-data processing.

prerequisites.reason: The exception must address a qualifying bias problem.

blocks: **Special categories of personal data** include particularly protected data such as health or racial/ethnic-origin information. Article 4a(1) permits exceptional processing by high-risk providers only to the extent strictly necessary for the specified bias detection and correction.

First show that other data, including synthetic or anonymised data, cannot effectively achieve the objective. Synthetic data is generated rather than collected from the actual person; anonymised data no longer identifies the person. Convenience or curiosity is not strict necessity. Applicable data-protection provisions continue to apply.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 4a(1)(a)–(f), (2); Article 10(2)(f), (g)

blocks: **Sensitive-bias safeguards** all apply: technical limits on reuse; state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures, including pseudonymisation; protected data with strict documented access only by authorised persons under confidentiality duties.

Pseudonymisation replaces identifying details while keeping the possibility of re-linking under protection; it is not anonymisation. A confidentiality promise alone does not establish the required access or technical measures.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 4a(1)(a)–(f), (2); Article 10(2)(f), (g)

blocks: The data must not be transmitted, transferred or otherwise accessed by other parties. Delete it when the bias is corrected or its retention period ends, whichever comes first.

The processing record must explain strict necessity and why other data could not achieve the objective. Sending the sensitive dataset to an external analytics supplier fails the no-other-party condition, even if that supplier signs confidentiality terms.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 4a(1)(a)–(f), (2); Article 10(2)(f), (g)

blocks: The **extended bias permission** in 4a(2) reaches other-system/model providers and deployers, including high-risk deployers, for strictly necessary correction of qualifying likely safety/rights/discrimination biases. Every paragraph 1 condition and safeguard still applies.
Paragraph 2 creates no new obligation to perform bias detection and correction. It is a conditional permission, not a general right to collect sensitive data and not an exemption from data law.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 4a(1)(a)–(f), (2); Article 10(2)(f), (g)

blocks: Case: Northbridge wants health information to investigate a specific suspected bias. Its file must substantiate necessity, failed alternatives, all protections, access limits, deletion timing and the data-law analysis.
If any required condition is absent, this exception is not established. Keep the proposal on hold under this route rather than treating a fairness aim as enough.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 4a(1)(a)–(f), (2); Article 10(2)(f), (g)
